record.prompt:
Build the first working version of the multiplayer game "neon-drift" from this starter repository (it only has a README and .gitignore). Two attachments are the binding contract: ENGINE.md (shared room engine, toolchain, file layout, protocol, safety, tests) and GAME.md (this game's rules). Follow them exactly; where they give exact versions, names or numbers, use those.

This is mission 1 of several. Its scope is the complete, correct ENGINE plus a minimal but real game loop:
- package.json (exact devDependencies and scripts from ENGINE.md), wrangler.jsonc, gitflare.json, migrations/0001_init.sql.
- src/index.ts (all routes incl. GET /health), src/room.ts (hibernation WebSockets, alarm-driven 30 Hz tick only while players are connected, reconnect tokens, spectators, rate limit, payload limit, lobby reporting), src/lobby.ts, src/leaderboard.ts (graceful without DB), src/room-logic.ts (pure, testable join/leave/reconnect/rate-limit helpers).
- public/shared/rng.js, public/shared/sim.js (the core rules of GAME.md: movement, the main collision rule, scoring basics, match phases), public/shared/protocol.js (compact arrays + delta codec against an acked baseline + full snapshot every 60 ticks).
- A minimal client: public/index.html, style.css, app.js (name field, Quick play, Create private room, /r/<CODE> join), net.js (WebSocket, join/reconnect with token, acks, ping), render.js (DPR-scaled canvas, rAF loop, draws the world from snapshots with 100 ms interpolation), input.js (keyboard + basic touch). Polish, particles and sound come in later missions, so keep render.js simple b
acceptanceCriteria: npm test passes with node:test tests covering deterministic replay, collision/scoring, input sanitisation, delta encode/apply round trip, name sanitisation, reconnect slot logic and the rate limiter.

wrangler.jsonc matches ENGINE.md: main src/index.ts, compatibility_date 2026-10-06, assets ./public with run_worker_first, ROOM and LOBBY Durable Objects with new_sqlite_classes migration, DB D1 binding with migrations_dir.
Room uses ctx.acceptWebSocket with serializeAttachment and an alarm-driven 30 Hz tick that stops when no players are connected.
Clients only send sequence-numbered inputs; the server sanitises them; snapshots are compact arrays with deltas against the acked baseline and a full snapshot on join and every 60 ticks.
Payload limit 2 KB, 60 msgs/s rate limit with disconnect at 3 strikes, names trimmed to 16 characters and rendered with textContent.
Reconnect with the issued token within 15 s keeps the player slot; full or finished rooms admit spectators.
GET /health returns { ok, rooms, players }; /api/leaderboard returns 200 with available:false when DB is missing.
Shared simulation is pure (no Date.now, Math.random, DOM or Workers APIs) and is imported by the Worker, the browser client and the tests.
The page loads with no inline scripts, renders a DPR-scaled canvas in one requestAnimationFrame loop, and the local player can join and move.
gitflare.json exists with install npm, test npm test and the editable list from the mission prompt.

reviews.body:
Blocking netcode issues found in review:

1. **Client drops most deltas.** `public/net.js` can only apply a delta whose `baseTick` equals the last or second-to-last received snapshot (`net.world` / `net.baseStore`). The server computes deltas against the client's last *acked* tick, which is RTT/33 ms ticks old (3-6 ticks at 100-200 ms RTT), so almost every delta hits `else return` and the client only updates on the full snapshot every 2 s. Keep a ring of the last 64 applied snapshots keyed by tick on the client (preallocated Map, delete tick-64), apply each delta to `ring.get(baseTick)`, and if the base is missing send `["a", -1]` (or simply keep acking) so the server falls back to a full snapshot. Add a test in a NEW file `tests/netcode.test.mjs` that simulates 5 ticks of ack latency: server ring + per-client lastAck, client ring, and asserts every delta applies and reproduces the server snapshot exactly.

2. **Message budget vs rate limit.** The client sends inputs at up to 30 Hz *and* a separate `["a", tick]` for every snapshot (30 Hz) *and* pings, i.e. >60 msgs/s, which collides with the 60 msgs/s limit and will strike honest players. Inputs already carry the ack tick as their last field: send a standalone ack only when no input was sent since the last snapshot, and at most 10 Hz. Make the server rate limiter a sliding/token bucket (60/s sustained, burst 90) rather than a fixed window reset, and add a test that a client sending 30 inputs/s + 10 acks/s + 1 ping/s for 10 simulated seconds never gets a strike.

3. **Server delta cost.** `encodeSnapshot` in `public/shared/protocol.js` copies and compares the whole trail prefix (`o.slice(2, 2+keep)`) for every trail for every client every tick (O(trail length x players x clients)). Use the trail's `trailBase` + point count to compute the appended range directly (points before the last one are immutable once pushed; only the head point moves), with no slicing of the prefix.

Keep everything else as is. Do not modify existing test files; add new tests in new files.

reviews.body:
Review of the combined candidate. Blocking:

**Netcode work missing.** The netcode retry only re-ran from the mission-1 scaffold and produced a one-line `-0` fix; the merged candidate has none of the netcode section of CONTRACT.md. Netcode agent: redo the whole netcode section now, starting from this merged candidate (the real rules sim.js, renderer and ui are present): makeSnapshot with cycles incl. meter and hue, counter-based trail append deltas (no per-tick array comparisons), quantised trail points with `|| 0` (no -0), orbs add/remove, arena/names extras, a snapshot for every stepped tick, one batched `["v", tick, ...events]` per tick, acks piggybacked on inputs and standalone acks ≤ 10 Hz, token bucket burst 90 with a strike per empty-bucket episode (≤ 1 per 250 ms) and close at 3, integer alarm scheduling, full snapshot < 4 KB at 16 players, and the full client net API (prediction in fixed DT steps through stepCycle with replay of unacked inputs, 100 ms interpolation, trails map with predicted local head). Add tests/netcode.test.mjs: trail deltas with 5 ticks of ack latency equal server trails, reconnect keeps the cycle, honest client never strikes, flood strikes and closes.

**Design pass (owner: "this UI looks like it was made in 1987")**
1. One screen at a time: `/` is the landing only; `/r/<code>` goes straight to a compact join sheet (name prefilled + Join) over a blurred live view of the arena (netcode: join field 5 = 1 means watch-only; a watcher may send a normal `["j", name, token, null]` on the same socket to become a player). After joining the arena fills the viewport; no landing remnants (`[hidden]{display:none!important}`).
2. Identity: neon synthwave arena, but designed: typography scale with a display stack ("Orbitron", "Eurostile", "Segoe UI", sans-serif; no downloads), HUD with structure — top-left player card (hue swatch, name, score, boost meter as a segmented bar), top-centre alive count and match timer with next-shrink countdown ring, kill feed bottom-left, minimap bottom-right, big centred 3-2-1 and "ELIMINATED — spectating <name>" banner, results panel with places. Glow only where it means something (trails, cycles, warnings); UI panels are flat glass with thin borders. No default browser buttons or bullet lists.
3. Empty/error states: leaderboard empty → "Be the first on the board"; real failure → error with retry. Local dev D1 must work: src/leaderboard.ts runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + indexes (same schema as migrations/0001_init.sql) once per isolate before the first query; README documents `wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --local` too. Live count shows "Be the first in the arena" at 0.
4. Mobile first: arena fills the screen, two large semi-transparent turn zones at the bottom corners plus a boost button (≥ 64 px) drawn by the renderer, HUD compacted to corners, works in portrait and landscape. Test at 390×844 and 1280×800.
5. Motion and sound: 150–250 ms transitions, camera kick and slow-mo (200 ms at 0.5×, client-side only) on your own elimination, prefers-reduced-motion respected.

Browser test of this candidate (wrangler dev 4.149.0, 4 bots + me). The new landing, join sheet over the blurred arena, HUD card and results panel look good. Integration bugs between your files (contract mismatches):

1. **Renderer crashes every frame**: `render.js:102` calls `net.names.get(id)` but `net.names` is a plain object (id → name) per CONTRACT.md: `Uncaught TypeError: net.names.get is not a function at drawCycle (render.js:102) at frame (render.js:184)`, hundreds per second. Use `net.names[id]`, and guard every net field the renderer reads. Owner: renderer.
2. **Watch-only join is not wired**: app.js calls `createNet(code, name, handlers, { watch: true })` and later `net.join(name)`, but net.js's `createNet(code, name, handlers)` ignores the 4th argument (it only reads `?watch=1` from the URL) and has no `join`. Result: opening `/r/<code>` immediately joins as a player named "Player", and typing a name does nothing. Implement `createNet(code, name, handlers, opts)` with `opts.watch` → join field 5 = 1, and `net.join(name)` sending `["j", name, token, null]` on the same socket; the server upgrades the watcher to a player with that name. Owner: netcode (net.js, room.ts).
3. **Results overlay stays up** after the next match starts ("Next match in 0 s" stays visible). Hide it whenever the phase is not `results`. Owner: ui.
4. Add a node test for each fix where possible (fake WebSocket for net.join; a stub net object with plain-object names for the renderer's name lookup helper), in new test files.

Browser test of this candidate (wrangler dev + bots). The names crash is fixed, the join sheet over the blurred live arena works, and the server-side upgrade works: a raw socket sending `["j","watcher",null,null,1]` then `["j","Upgraded",null,null]` receives a second welcome with role `player` and the cycle named "Upgraded". Remaining:

1. **Client stays a spectator after Join**: in the browser, after typing a name and pressing Join, the HUD keeps the "spectating" badge and shows "0 / 0 alive"; steering does nothing. net.js must treat the second `w` message as a full reset to player mode: set `net.id`, `net.role = 'player'`, store the new token, clear and re-seed the snapshot ring from the welcome's full snapshot, reset prediction state, and notify `handlers.welcome` so app.js hides the badge. Add a node test with a fake WebSocket that sends a spectator welcome then a player welcome and asserts `net.role === 'player'`, `net.id` set and `net.me` non-null after the next snapshot (new test file). (netcode)
2. **Desktop shows a big touch boost ring** in the bottom-right corner. Draw touch controls only when `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches` or after a touch event. (renderer)
3. **Server stall once**: with 4 bots and a browser connected for a few minutes, the local Worker stopped answering every request (even `/health` and static assets) until restarted; not reproduced in a 40 s retest. IN  ["v",328,["crash",3,-1,...],["phase","results"],["results",[...]]]
OUT ["j","Player",null,null]
IN  ["w",4,"f9ee9ffa…","DRFT26","spectator",462,["results",…]]

Players who joined (or upgraded from watch-only) while the room was `results` or full keep a reserved seat: when the next `countdown` begins and there is space (≤ 16), promote them in join order: add their cycle to the sim, send them a fresh `["w", id, token, code, "player", tick, full]` and report to the Lobby.
